title: Microsoft Unveils Its First Speech-to-Speech Model MAI Realtime 1: It Can Be Interrupted, Make Calls and Get Work Done, at Only One-Third the Price of Competitors
excerpt: Yesterday (November 17) at the Ignite 2026 conference, Microsoft unveiled MAI Realtime 1, its first speech-to-speech model, built for real-world enterprise scen
content_html:
Yesterday (November 17) at the Ignite 2026 conference, Microsoft unveiled MAI Realtime 1, its first speech-to-speech model, built for real-world enterprise scenarios. It can handle conversational details such as interruptions, quick acknowledgments, and waiting for the other person to finish, and it can understand requests in noisy environments or when multiple people are speaking at once. When a task requires deeper thinking, it can call on a stronger reasoning engine and connect to enterprise systems to complete operations such as bookings and customer service handling. Its tone and style can be tuned with prompts.

The price sheet is shockingly disruptive
